summary: This program stores an item name and its price in variables, then builds a single sentence from them using an f-string. An f-string lets you drop variable values directly into text without stitching pieces together by hand.

lines.text: The name of the product is stored as a string, in quotation marks, so it can be reused in the message below.
The price is a float, Python's type for numbers with a decimal point, which is what money amounts need.

The f before the opening quote marks this as an f-string, so Python replaces {item} and {price} with the values of those variables. The dollar sign before {price} is ordinary text and is printed as-is, because only names inside braces get substituted.
